subject: Performance gating checklist & MAP commitment — Redwood variant tradeoffs
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP request — performance gates + variant guidance

Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — Acme is moving to a firm close on the provider selection and procurement wants a short MAP that includes performance gating for the classifier we plan to run in prod. High level asks below:

- Target use case: clinical triage classifier (short clinical notes, avg input 120 tokens)
- Acceptance gates we need in MAP: p95 latency (TTFT+stream) <= 250ms; sustained throughput >= 110 req/s at concurrency 64; warm TTFT under 80ms; token-cost budget target < $0.0009/token for the expected request mix.
- Need a side-by-side variant comparison: at minimum include two candidate variants that balance quality vs perf; quality measure = macro-F1 on our 6-class taxonomy (we can share eval set).
- Timing: can you provide a MAP with benchmarking plan and preliminary results by EOD 2027-06-20? Procurement needs the performance gating language for the SOW.

If you need the eval set or a short prompt set, I can share a redacted sample. Also loop in contracts for the procurement language.

Sam
Sam Jenkins
Director of AI Products | Acme Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Contracts Team <contracts@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP request — performance gates + variant guidance

Sam — thanks for the clear ask. Below is the MAP-oriented plan and the benchmarking checklist we will use. I attached a compact perf matrix (MAP_perf_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a subset of eval prompts we used for the pilot.

MAP milestones (timeline to EOD 2027-06-20):
1) 6/15-6/16: ingest redacted eval set and confirm tokenization / preprocessing with Acme. Owner: Marissa.
2) 6/16-6/18: run controlled perf sweep across variants at target concurrency profiles (32, 64, 128). Owner: Marissa + infra.
3) 6/18-6/19: quality eval (macro-F1) on held-out prompts, calibrate temperature + sampling. Owner: Karthik + Marissa.
4) 6/19: consolidate results + generate gating language for SOW. Owner: Karthik.
5) 6/20: MAP delivery + stakeholder sync (30m).

Benchmarking checklist (what we'll measure):
- Cold start TTFT (first request after idle 30m) and warm TTFT (steady-state).
- p50/p95/p99 latency for inference and end-to-end TTFT.
- Sustained throughput at target concurrency levels (success rate, error rate).
- Memory / GPU utilization and quantization profile used.
- Cost per 1k tokens and cost per inference (estimated).

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Pass if candidate variant meets p95 <= 250ms AND macro-F1 within 1.5 points of baseline (Acme's target) AND throughput >= 110 req/s at concurrency 64 with <1% errors.
- If none pass, define fallback policy (smaller model + batching) and list recommended mitigations.

I'll run the first perf sweep tonight and push results tomorrow. If there are any additional constraints from procurement (e.g., minimum token-retention or logging) flag them to me and Contracts.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-17T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP request — performance gates + variant guidance

Karthik / Sam — quick update from the perf runs (attached: variant_latency_histograms.png + MAP_perf_matrix_v1.xlsx). Summary of the controlled sweep (single-GPU serving config, quantized weights where noted):

Candidates tested:
- rw-llama-7b-q4 (Q4 quantized 7B)
  - p95 TTFT: 180ms (warm), cold TTFT: 320ms
  - Sustained throughput @ concurrency 64: 130 req/s (error rate 0.3%)
  - Macro-F1 (6-class): 86.2% on Acme eval subset
  - Estimated token cost: $0.00065/token

- rw-llama-13b-q4 (Q4 quantized 13B)
  - p95 TTFT: 260ms (warm), cold TTFT: 460ms
  - Sustained throughput @ concurrency 64:  ninety-two (92) req/s (error rate 0.6%)
  - Macro-F1 (6-class): 88.9% on Acme eval subset
  - Estimated token cost: $0.00095/token

Interpretation: the 7B variant comfortably meets the p95 <= 250ms and throughput target; quality is ~2.7 points lower than the 13B. The 13B shows a clear quality lift but misses the latency/throughput gates at the current serving config.

Next steps I propose (to include in MAP):
- Recommend rw-llama-7b-q4 as the initial go-live variant with conservative batch sizing to keep p95 headroom.
- Define staged rollout: start with 7B for first 2 weeks, collect live quality signals on production traffic; if macro-F1 meets threshold and cost is acceptable, enable 13B for high-importance flows via routing policy (canary A/B).
- Add fallback: if p95 climbs above 300ms, automatic traffic shift to 7B and notify on-call.

I'll attach the exact run configs and a short set of eval prompts (eval_prompts_subset.jsonl) so Acme can reproduce locally if needed.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Contracts Team <contracts@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP request — performance gates + variant guidance

Thanks Marissa — this is the right level of detail. A couple quick operational notes for procurement language:

- We'll propose the acceptance gate exactly as written (p95 <= 250ms, throughput >= 110 req/s, macro-F1 within 1.5 pts) and include measurement method (weighted mix of 80/20 clinical/operational prompts, 30m sampling window, 3 sequential runs to reduce variance).
- Contracts: please add text that allows Redwood to provide traceable benchmark reports and run artifacts as evidence. Also include the staged-rollout fallback and notification SLAs.
- Commercial: we can offer a one-week trial SLA extension (reduced price credit) if the staged rollout shows regressions; that'll smooth the close.

If that reads OK to Acme, Karthik — let's finalize the MAP doc and I'll ask Legal to prepare the SOW appendix.

Hannah Schmitt
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP request — performance gates + variant guidance

All — this looks good and actionable. Appreciate the clear recommendation.

Acme accepts the proposal to start on rw-llama-7b-q4 with the staged rollout to 13B for high-importance flows. Please include the exact measurement method in the SOW appendix (as Hannah noted) and provide the benchmarking artifacts by EOD tomorrow so procurement can finalize the SOW.

I'll upload the redacted eval set to the Drive link you provided and loop in our Contracts lead (contracts@acmehealth.com) with any final questions.

Sam
Sam Jenkins
Director of AI Products | Acme Health
